A worthy successor to the previous game, reiterating on the formula by introducing a rougelite twist akin to the last game's DLC. However, the humor falls flat compared to the first game, akin to the modern Marvel "well, this is awkward" and "I TALK LOUD SO I'M FUNNY" type. The soundtrack is great, the gameplay is responsive although sometimess the aiming seems somewhat off, the final boos fight/late game stretch is a slog where a mistake or two sends you back quite a ways. Troony toons propaganda showed in nonsensically, appearing even in the final boss. However, there's some irony in Turnip Boy fighting and defeating the extraterrestrial last boss that shoots necromorph lasers, which probably gave me a chuckle along with one sidequest where a character sends a response to another one in a letter on which only "based" is written. Other than that, there's barely any humor to be had in a game that takes itself none too seriously.

I am genuinely sad to write this review. I loved the first turnip boy game, but I cannot give this game a positive review. Where do I start? *This is a mostly spoiler free review, any spoilers will be marked as such* [h2] Main Gameplay [/h2] I don't think the gameplay is bad neither because it's different from TBCTE, nor because I don't like topdown shooters. I think the gameplay is bad because there is just way too much going on. A lot of the main ideas feel like they were added really early in development and never expanded upon. There are many examples for this, such as: The timer. The timer just feels like an annoyance, you never feel any sense of urgency to get back to the car up until you reach the max star rating and *very minor mechanics spoiler* [spoiler] start taking forced damage [/spoiler], which is honestly just a very lazy way to make the player stop their current heist rather than introducing a more fun risk/reward mechanic to the game. There are some other minor gameplay issues this game has, such as melee attacks from enemies being borderline undodgeable and copious amounts of screenshake when firing certain weapons, but also another big issue: bosses. Bosses are just DPS races and bullet sponges, all (except for one) spend half of their fight being completely invincible (which makes half of the fight incredibly boring) and the amount of enemies they spawn during that time makes it more or less impossible to dodge everything. Every boss (apart from *mid-endgame spoiler* [spoiler]the burger guy[/spoiler], which wasn't that bad honestly) feels very same-y. Apart from their sprites, dialogue and some attacks there's nothing that makes them unique. The final "boss" is a whole different can of worms, I'll talk about that in the part of the review discussing the ending. Another big problem this game has is the money system. This part of the review is probably better as its own section: [h2] Progression [/h2] Progression doesn't feel satisfying. Doing the things integral to a fun and engaging gameplay loop like killing enemies rewards you with not nearly enough money. Instead, 95% of the money I got during my playthrough were from these "pedestal items". This would be fine if I got them just from vaults (dungeons) as a reward, but they are also just laying around in a random area. To make matters even worse, getting into a new area gives better items, which makes sense in providing a sense of progression. However, this makes all previously collected money completely useless, as the values of the items in the next area are multiplied by ten. This once again results in the gameplay being affected (you just run past any and all enemies and pick up pedestal items, any time spent killing enemies feels like a waste of time) and in progression not feeling meaningful, since upgrades feel expensive in one area with worse items and extremely cheap in the next area with much better items. On the topic of upgrades, they just aren't interesting. Upgrades just boil down to "More Health" and "More Damage". The other progression mechanic is an exchange of the money mechanic for story progression which as mentioned above just doesn't work, and the third one is just a way to slap more time on this very short game, more on that later. With this last upgrade mechanic, you can unlock new weapons by bringing the NPC weapons you found in the bank from enemy drops. The problem is that half of the weapons you unlock are complete and utter garbage DPS-wise, not making it worth to invest time in the system. Alright, next section. [h2]Main Quest/Story[/h2] If you've played TBCTE the story is pretty much what you'd expect. Nothing much I can elaborate on here. It's pretty much "Go to area A, kill boss, unlock progression item, go to next area". There's a bunch of goofy lore sprinkled in here and there and the jokes are pretty funny, but that's about it. The ending however... [h2]Ending[/h2] *obviously spoilers* [spoiler] The ending just feels so incredibly random, even accounting for the whacky ahh story the first game had... And don't get me started on the final boss/ending sequence. The sequence is just so unnecessarily punishing and difficult. The ending sequence forces you to redo every boss again, which could be a fun way to show how much stronger/better you've gotten, but you have to do it every. single. time. you die in the final sequence. The ending sequence is a chase sequence through the entire map but in space. (This highlights another issue I'll pick up after I write down everything about the ending.) The chase sequence is way too difficult for the game. I'm no stranger to hard games, but this is not what turnip boy is meant to be. All attacks from the boss do way too much damage and you can't really do anything against the boss other that running away from them. When I completed this section after like 7 attempts, it just felt like complete luck.[/spoiler] [h2]Side Quests and Grinding[/h2] Why did I put these two things into the same section? Well, some of the quests *NPCs that give you side quests spoiler* [spoiler]the mushroom cultists and DJ sizzle [/spoiler] just end up as very grindy and annoying. You have to *spoiler for quests* [spoiler]literally kill 200 enemies of one type for multiple quests and kill 200 enemies with a specific weapon for another one[/spoiler] what I would get if these were accessible from the earlygame, providing another sense of progression by slowly completing the requirements for these quests, but they are deliberately locked behind a lategame area, which just makes them feel like filler for this very short game. I completed the main story after three hours while completing some of the shorter and easier side quests along the way, but I spent the other two hours completing the side quests mentioned above and the starting weapon arsenal which is once again just a complete grindfest. The *very minor mechanics spoiler* [spoiler] randomized elevator doors [/spoiler] just make it all the more annoying to find one specific quest NPC. [h2]The other things I don't have a specific section for[/h2] Why is the game so short? I don't mind short games at all, but come on! 15€ for 5 Hours, almost half of which I spent grinding for 100%? The game is trying too hard to be a sequel in some areas of the story *ending spoiler* [spoiler]oh look the final section is in space, it's just like the first game oh wow[/spoiler] Why can't I change the aspect ratio? The music still slaps, but why aren't there any specific boss/area themes anymore? [h2]TL;DR:[/h2] If you liked TBCTE for its humor, you might like this game, but it's still watered down by a mediocre at best, somehow both grindy and short playing experience. It fails to establish a proper gameplay loop and somehow actively punishes players for interacting with its mechanics. Thanks for reading this absolute wall of text by the way, dear devs, if you read this, please keep this in mind if you ever make TB3

Man, i really liked the first Game. It was different, Colorful, sometimes Dark, but most importantly just innocent Fun. This Game here also isnt that bad, even tho im no Fan of Bullet Hell Games, even tho this one is a quite easy one, atleast if you want it to be easy. But i also dislike the constant backtracking and FOMO. What also bothers me is, that while this is clearly a Game that makes Fun of basicly everything in our society, but lets be honest. Life is just a huge Circus and we are the Actors. I dont understand how someone would put a Trans Flag into the Game. Is this Supposed to be a Joke? Is this a Statement? A Message? Was the Person Serious? No matter how you take it, first and foremost, it doesnt fit or belong into such a Game. You cant be satirical about basicly anything and then be totally serious. Thats not how anything of this Works. And Secondly, i deeply dislike getting Opinions and Statements of others shoved into my Face. Having an Opinion is good. But dont make it other Peoples Problems. I am part of this stuff myself, and i hate these Attention ♥♥♥♥♥ People who have to tell the entire World that they are Special. stop making us look like Clowns and Attention ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Im sick of these Attention Hungry People. That being said, like mentioned earlier. the Game itself is quite solid. Nothing Special. I would have prefered a Game like the first one waaay more. You know, a Game more akin to old Zelda Games rather than being a Repetetive backtracking Fomo Bullet Hell Game. What bothers me also quite much is, in the first Game you had a quite slow, but still steady Pacing but not too slow so that i never got boring, but also didnt overloaded you with stuff. This Game here, is even slower. Sure.. the shooting and Movement is faster. But the Story is a lot slower, just like the Jokes and Humor overall. simply because of the repetetive Nature of the Game. I had high hopes for this Game and also for the Devs, that they would be on a similar Level like "The Behemoth". But sadly, as of now, they arent.. anymore. They should have just done their Taxes, maybe this would have helped. :( !!!

My opinion of this game is very "meh", if I am being honest. To start with, the combat is pretty simplistic, but still workable. The weapons can be pretty cool, although the weapon balancing is admittedly all over the place, and some weapons can randomly be a lot stronger than others, sometimes even being as strong as endgame weapons. Or the weapon dropped by the Area 3 and 4 bosses for example. which as weapons are a lot weaker than those dropped by the area 1 and 2 bosses. This is a game about speed after all, and having a slow weapon with medium damage from endgame bosses can feel extremely underwhelming. Moving onto the next topic, ths speed. While this game isn't that bad of a videogame generally, I can say with certainly that it feels like the creators of this game do not understand what a roguelike is. No stats are gained or any real choices are made besides "what guns do you have", or "how much money you gain", though the former is pretty discouraged by the fact you can just keep your favorite guns in lockers all the time, and you won't really have to try to get some of the best weapons in the game. I wish it was a bit more difficult, and I wish the devs properly understood what a roguelike is before making this game. Not that bad of a game personally, but it is a bit bad when it is marked as a game with a lot of replayability when in reality its replayability is almost nil by the time you have beaten the final boss, which is not at all what a roguelike should be like.

从村霸大头菜一代过来了！二代出来后首发就买了直到今天才给通关，开头就说大头菜是奇才笑死我了一代屠了火车这代来屠银行 定价58的内容感觉有些少大概5个小时就全成就了不知道后面会不会出dlc或者扩展之类的，本作主要是带有肉鸽性质的刷图刷武器然后一边抢银行劫财毁坏家具无恶不作———要说优点感觉就是人物走路速度像是开了1.5倍加速一样快，甚至有时候视力都跟不上人物速度这一点很爽不会有很墨迹的地方，人物对话也可以快速跳过（抱歉！！有些对话还是很有意思的，每个人说话很口语话甚至有的还非主流有一种小脑缺失自言自语但又带点幽默的美，而且制作人里应该是有JO厨我记得一代还有花京院的reoreoreo樱桃梗）其次就是武器种类还是蛮有意思的，我拿的是手柄玩的，因为有很多远程武器所以手柄玩会有些吃力更多用的是近战武器（前期刷到DJ房拿个镰刀可以说是无敌了） 缺点的话也很明显，首先地图不够大，肉鸽房也相对单一甚至有的后期完成支线可以说是完全没用了，怪物的种类比较少，BOSS可以重复打不过没啥奖励机制打过一次就想打第二次了（好像会掉BOSS专属武器但是个人觉得并不好用）建议还是打折买，个人觉得30元以下可以无脑冲因为确实本作主打一个抢银行爽，每一局结束看自己赚了多少钱还是很有成就感的， 剧情相对简单也很无厘头搞笑，比如做支线的一个不起眼的小NPC居然是我们大反派的儿子，比如我们的黄瓜老大从要当坏人突然就开始变成对抗外星人的英雄了，比如吸血鬼突然就对非主流地雷魔鬼女王一见钟情，比如我们没背景的大头菜突然就有了爸爸姐姐的背景（？）在这个过程里总是会有很离谱但又很好笑的事情，后面会拿到爸爸的遗物的手枪，捡到后爸爸的亡灵会跟在我的身后我为了升级武器转手就卖了（抱歉）以及很喜欢每次开头一个卡车突然闯进银行的那种感觉很大杀四方！ 成就相对比较简单只要肝刷就完事了，比较麻烦的是支线任务要杀够多少个桃子警察这个最好在倒计时到了的时候满屋子乱走会刷出好多可以趁这个时候杀，任务都在手机里记得多拿出手机看看！ 最后经历两代我才知道我们的大头菜是萌妹！！（游戏里会有NPC画娘化的大头菜肖像）好可爱，好可爱！用最可爱的表情拿着最凶残的武器做出最血腥的事！！大头菜好！像素风好！

tl;dr: 7/10 + improved fighting system + interesting exploration + the artstyle and music were fantastic + rich in humor and creative commentary - there’s no post-game content - semi-random aspects may be tedious to interact with - glitched achievement system xD The second installment in the Turnip Boy series, and oh boy, it was a pleasure. The game maintains the RPG-style of the previous game, but this time, focuses more on combat and exploration. I liked the combat system - when compared to the previous game, it presents way more different options for both melee and shooting weapons. The enemies were also more demanding and more numerous, turning the game into bullet hell in some cases. I wish the portal weapon was kept from the ‘Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evansion’. Also, I was surprised that there’s no post-game content, similar to the ‘Limitless Line’ known from the previous installment. Sure, you can replay the boss battles and wander through the whole map after finishing the game, but that gets boring and repetitive almost instantly. This also applies to the money Turnip Boy gathers - after buying out every upgrade and quest item, there’s no point in gathering more treasure. The exploration part was fun - it was connected with a timer, after which more enemies spawned. Adjacent to the main building, there were several semi-randomly generated areas, which offered bonus quests or content. These were super exciting to explore. However, I wish there was a method of controlling where exact room spawns - in the late game, I had a few quests to finish in there, so I just kept reloading the level until they appeared. The artstyle and music were quite creative, and also “cweative UwU :33”. I especially liked the portrayal of the game's soundtrack as an mp3 player, where we could change the playlist, or add new songs via quests. The game was also soaking with humor and references to different social phenomena, somewhat in the South Park-esque style. TBRaB was smooth and worked fluently. There was one minor problem with lightning during the gameplay (namely, one of the weapons acted like a torch, but sometimes did not emit the light properly - thankfully, after reloading it, everything worked fine). I had a problem with the achievements - I wanted to 100% the game and its achievements on Steam, but unfortunately, one of the last tasks glitched and I did not get my award 😂😂 xD. Overall, this game was a pleasure and a quite relaxing experience. It was relatively short, but perfect for binge gaming. It deserves a solid 7/10.

This game(a forced multirun progression game with grinding) is not nearly as good as the first(an adventure game with some minor puzzles). The combat and writing are pretty much the same, and I enjoyed it at first, then became annoyed with the gameplay loop, then frustrated with the randomness and design meant to waste the player's time. This game has no puzzles, replacing them with fetch quests and grind. Want a new starting weapon? Pick up weapons dropped in a run(max two at a time), bring it back, and get a tiny bit of exp towards it. Want upgrades because you feel weak? Get money from a run, bring it back to maybe purchase one. Want to progress the story? Reach a certain point, get an item unlocked for sale, end the run to go back to base and see how much it costs, and go back into the level to grind if you don't have enough. Given a task to find something? It's either going to be a reward from another fetch quest, an item you need to leave your run to buy, grind enemies, or run for a minute elsewhere to progress it. Or, my absolute least favorite, it's in the tree that looks the same as the other trees except there's an easy to miss interact prompt on it. This is not a rogue-like. The runs are the same layouts, the same enemies. The only thing randomized each run is the location of certain quest rooms, so first you have to get lucky enough for the elevator to spawn said room, go in to start the task, and more than likely finish the run with it incomplete. (Most tasks boil down to talking to the quest-giver, then progressing through the game until you hit the person/thing who has your item, then getting it, then praying the game spawns the room you need. It's truly terrible when these special rooms have rewards that let you advance another random-room's quest.) Then get the item, and hope the game some day lets the room spawn again so you can turn it in. The bosses, should you die to them, require you to watch their slow, typed character by character, cutscene every time you want to refight them, not to mention any sort of runback you have to do to reach them(thankfully, the final boss at least [spoiler]leaves the other bosses from the boss rush dead, though that does mean farming weapon exp should be done before going for him.[/spoiler]) Other than the final boss, they are fairly simple fights, and if you've been unlocking weapons, you should be able to win on your first or second try. But the final boss is just a bad design. [spoiler]He covers a significant portion of the screen at times, is in the foreground so he hides you, enemies and obstacles(meaning you get stuck/take a lot of damage quickly), and his attacks can be unavoidable if he catches you in certain terrain. Plus, for a game with a ton of combat, you don't actually fight him. You run away. Good news is that the primary 'antagonist' has nothing to do with the final boss and just runs off when you initially confront him, so no closure there either.[/spoiler] Story-wise, don't expect the level of the first one. The layers are much shallower here, casually tossed in and thin. Does have a decent ending for Turnip Boy though. The writing is similar humor-wise though, so that's fun. Of my playtime, a good chunk was grind, trying to get a room to spawn, and dealing with the final boss. That is not what I want in a game.
